item: The session sentinel (session_state.json) is written through a copy named for the process and the thread, so two servers on one data folder can no longer tear it or lose a swap
summary: forensics._write_state wrote session_state.json through the one fixed copy name session_state.json.tmp, which every server on a data folder (R176) shared: the second writer truncated the first's open file and the first swap moved that half-written file into place (a mixture of two states in the sentinel the next boot reads), or the second's swap found nothing to move and its state was lost with a warning. Measured on the old writer with two threads standing in for two servers. The copy is now session_state.json.<pid>.<thread>.part, synced before the swap and removed if the swap fails (the shape of collect_perf._trim_jsonl, R175); the last swap wins as before; a copy a killed process left is removed by the next write once that pid is gone (psutil imported only when another process's copy is there). 13 tests in tests/test_forensics_state_write.py: 6 fail on the old writer (the half-way writer, the lost swap, a refused swap leaving its copy, the sync-before-swap order, the per-thread name, the dead-copy removal), 7 are controls that pass on both (bytes, the kill-at-write and kill-at-swap old-sentinel-whole, a copy that cannot be serialised, no-psutil leaves the copy, no-psutil says so once); 9 mutants caught (shared name, no sync, no sweep, sweep removes live copies, no cleanup on failure, thread dropped from the name, log on every write, never log, raise when psutil is missing). Stated: this is the R175 shape, not the R176 conversion (the read-modify-write is not under file_lock; the allowance in test_shared_file_writes.py drops from 2 sites to 1); an older-version server still swaps the old fixed name; the sync on the shutdown path was not measured on a loaded disk.
